keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. 'In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan and forced the Hephthalite principalities to submit'; Tardush Shad 'controlled all the new Turk realm south of the Oxus, from his capital at Kunduz'; the maximum-extent map is 'circa 625-652'. The Kunduz core is drawn here and the rest of Tokharistan is left to the Western Turks (western-gokturks gain of 625), who give it to the Yabghus in 657. The page gives no area.

correction.text: Tokharistan south of the Oxus, reaching Badakhshan in the east and Bamiyan in the south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Tokharistan corresponds to the upper Oxus valley'; 'The area reaches east as far as the Badakshan mountains, south as far as Bamiyan'; 'Arab sources considered Kabul as part of the southern border of Tokharistan, and Shaganiyan as part of its northern border'; 'In a narrow sense, Tokharistan may only refer to the region south of the Oxus.' The southern, narrow Tokharistan is drawn; Chaghaniyan, Khuttal and Kapisa-Gandhara are vassals from 718.

correction.text: Badakhshan, the remnant of the Yabghus

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 710, Qutaiba ibn Muslim was able to re-establish Muslim control over Tokharistan'; the Yabghu was exiled to Damascus; 'Remnants survived in the area of Badakhshan until 758 CE.'

ledger.note: 625: Tong Yabgu invades Tokharistan and installs his son Tardush Shad at Kunduz. 'In 625, Tong Yabgu invaded Tokharistan and forced the Hephthalite principalities to submit'; infobox 'Established: 625 CE', capital Kunduz.

652-653: the Arabs overrun Tokharistan. 'In 652-653 CE, the Arabs under Abdallah ibn Amir conquered the whole of Tokharistan.' The Yabghus survive: they are under the Tang protectorate from 659 and send envoys in 758.

653: the Arab campaign ends. The page gives 652-653 as one conquest and shows the Yabghus still reigning at Kunduz under Tang suzerainty, so the contest is closed at the end of the span (confidence 2).

region.text: Tokharistan south of the Oxus and Badakhshan

ledger.note: 657: the Western Turkic Khaganate falls and Tokharistan is the Yabghus' own. 'The Western Turkic Khaganate itself was destroyed by the Tang dynasty in 657 CE'; 'After 650, the Yabghus came, at least partially, under Tang suzerainty.'

region.text: Tokharistan south of the Oxus without Badakhshan

ledger.note: 710: Qutayba re-establishes Muslim control. 'In 710, Qutaiba ibn Muslim was able to re-establish Muslim control over Tokharistan.' The Yabghu was exiled to Damascus; the remnants kept Badakhshan.

region.text: Khuttal, Chaghanian, Kabul and Zabul: the Yabghu 'ruled a vast area circa 718 CE' 'formed of the territories north and south of the Hindu Kush, including the areas of Kabul and Zabul'

ledger.note: 718: the Chinese account of 718 lists Khuttal, Chaghanian, Kabul and Zabul under the Yabghu. The page: Puluo's account in the Cefu Yuangui (718) 'shows that the Yabghu of Tokharistan ruled a vast area circa 718 CE', 'formed of the territories north and south of the Hindu Kush, including the areas of Kabul and Zabul'; its list names 'the king of [Zabul]', 'the king of [Kabul]', 'Khuttal' and 'Chaghanian' among others. The page does not date the start of the relation. [Reviewer ia-01-x, 2026-10-19] region and counterpart corrected: the 718 list names Kabul and Zabul, not Kapisa-Gandhara (Kapisa-Gandhara is the 625 list).

region.text: Khuttal, Chaghanian, Kabul and Zabul: the Yabghu 'ruled a vast area circa 718 CE' 'formed of the territories north and south of the Hindu Kush, including the areas of Kabul and Zabul'

ledger.note: 758: the Yabghu's last embassy. 'In 758 CE Wu-na-to (Udita?) visited in person the Chinese court'; the page dates no end to the Yabghu's overlordship, so the end of the dossier is the bridge (confidence 1).
758: the Yabghus end. Infobox 'Disestablished: 758 CE'; 'Remnants survived in the area of Badakhshan until 758 CE'; the page's successors are the Tang dynasty and the Turk Shahis.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Yabghus; the western-gokturks dossier already uses the counterpart 'tokhara-yabghus' for 657). The western-gokturks dossier draws Tokharistan south of the Oxus as Western Turk land from 625 to 656 (its 625 gain) and the Yabghus from 657, so this dossier's 625 keyframe is only the Kunduz core and the full shape is from 657. The Tang suzerainty (the 659 list of the Protectorate page, which names Tokharistan and Kabul among the states that submitted) is the Tang dossier's vassal_start, not an event here. The page gives no date for the Yuezhi Area Command at Kunduz, no Turgesh role and no last yabghu's name. The 710 loss to the Umayyads is not repeated for the Chaghaniyan and Khuttal vassals, whose relation the page dates only from the Chinese list of 718. No area. The Alchon Huns dossier has the Western Turks take Kapisa-Gandhara in 625; the 718 vassal tint here overlaps the Turk Shahis. Gazetteer names used (Bactria, Badakhshan, Kondoz, Khatlon, Surkhandarya, Kapisa, Gandhara) resolve. [Reviewer ia-01-x, 2026-10-19] The 718 vassal tint now names Kabul and Zabul (Kabulistan, Zabulistan) as the page's 718 account does; Gandhara is out. Cliopatria's Turk Shahis shapes of 644-717 (bbox to 38.4 N) also cover Tokharistan: 85 percent of keyframe tokhara-yabghus_657 lies inside the Turk Shahi shape of 680, so the two double-draw 657-709 until the turk-shahis dossier (not yet written) takes its northern edge back to the Hindu Kush.
